briefing.opening: Good day. I will now begin the climate briefing for August 17, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Extreme Climate Phenomena and Unprecedented Impacts
sections.content:
Today, we are confronted with extreme climate phenomena that clearly demonstrate the severity of the climate crisis. In particular, Geoje and Tongyeong in Gyeongsangnam-do experienced a record-breaking downpour of 654mm in a single day today, the last day of the Liberation Day holiday, leading to landslides, flood damage, and even casualties, prompting the issuance of a national fire mobilization order [27]. This 'climate whiplash,' characterized by extreme shifts between drought and heavy rainfall within three days, has been observed in various regions across the country, with global warming identified as a primary cause [6, 11]. Climate disasters such as heatwaves and heavy rains have severely impacted the daily lives of socially vulnerable groups, with many unable to go outside or experiencing social isolation [28].

Internationally, Europe's agricultural sector faces an 'unprecedented crisis' due to successive heatwaves and severe droughts, with France's vegetable production significantly decreasing compared to the previous year [10, 68]. Record-early harvests in French Champagne vineyards have highlighted the impacts of climate change [30, 57]. The Western United States is experiencing intensified water shortages, with severe snow droughts and two major reservoirs reaching record-low levels [31, 73], while large-scale wildfires in Belgium and Spain prompted the deployment of European Union support [69].

These climate changes are also having immense impacts on ecosystems. The discovery of a rare hammerhead shark suggests a potential reorganization of shark habitats [33], and five 'forgotten' endangered species, along with over 40% (more than 300 species) of American amphibians, are threatened by climate change [59, 64]. In Colorado, heat-related illnesses have surged amidst record temperatures, and a Lancet Public Health study indicates that adults over 60 face health risks from heat exposure even at lower temperatures than previously anticipated, once again emphasizing the urgency of climate crisis response [38, 44, 67].

sections.title: 🌱 Climate Action and Strengthening Policy Efforts
sections.content:
Amidst this crisis, diverse policy and technological efforts, both domestic and international, continue in response to climate change. The Korea Climate Change Research Institute is expanding international cooperation for greenhouse gas reduction in developing countries, contributing to global climate action [3], and inter-state cooperation is active, with Vietnam and Singapore implementing agreements on Article 6 of the Paris Agreement [12]. Domestically, Cheorwon-gun has commenced the establishment of a master plan to proactively prevent drought concerns [9], and Goyang Special City and the Gyeongsanwon-Yangpyeong-gun Energy Cooperative are strengthening cooperation for eco-friendly energy transition and dissemination [22, 24].

Policy and technology development for achieving carbon neutrality goals are also actively underway. The Carbon Neutrality Framework Act, which includes reduction pathways beyond 2030, has passed the National Assembly, expected to alleviate the government's burden of greenhouse gas reduction and influence corporate target setting [14, 16, 17]. CATL has set a roadmap to achieve carbon neutrality targets in its core operations by 2025 and value chain targets by 2035 [15], while Korea, through the SEED Initiative, is intensively fostering Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) and nuclear fusion technologies to simultaneously address AI power shortages and carbon neutrality [19]. Furthermore, KCL is strengthening its Zero Energy Building (ZEB) certification capabilities, leading the dissemination of carbon-neutral technologies [18].

Significant progress is also being made in investments and institutional improvements for expanding renewable energy infrastructure. Over the past five years, 1.3 trillion won has been invested in renewable energy transmission and substation facilities [20], and the launch of a single window for renewable energy permits is anticipated in 2027, expected to streamline related procedures [23]. In Europe, grid guidelines are being established to resolve bottlenecks in renewable energy transition, demonstrating multifaceted efforts in climate change adaptation and mitigation through international cooperation and technological development [25]. The German Social Democratic Party is pushing for a constitutional amendment to address heatwaves and the climate crisis [55], Pacific farms are adapting to climate change using traditional knowledge [54], and an analysis showing a one-third reduction in land-use emissions this century is interpreted as a positive sign [74].

sections.title: 📰 Complex Challenges of Energy Transition
sections.content:
Climate change, war, and artificial intelligence (AI) are ultimately converging into a single core phenomenon: the 'energy problem' [1, 65]. This suggests that ensuring the stability and sustainability of energy systems is one of the greatest challenges currently facing humanity. Obstacles to renewable energy expansion are also emerging during the energy transition; in China, cases of large quantities of clean power being curtailed due to grid limitations have been reported, raising concerns about hindering global renewable energy dissemination [21].

In this context, Korea is pursuing a strategy through the SEED Initiative to foster SMR and nuclear fusion technologies, aiming to simultaneously meet the increasing power demand of the AI era and achieve carbon neutrality goals [19]. Furthermore, efforts to improve infrastructure, including large-scale investments in renewable energy transmission and substation facilities and the establishment of a single window for renewable energy permits in 2027, aim to resolve bottlenecks in the energy transition [20, 23]. In Europe, movements to enhance the efficiency of renewable energy transition through grid guidelines are also observed [25].

Global conflicts and climate change are driving up shipping costs, exacerbating the instability of energy supply chains [37], and news of a new 'ice silk road' emerging in the Arctic also suggests the potential impacts and changes climate change could have on energy transportation routes [47]. Thus, energy proves to be a critical driving force in overcoming the climate crisis, while simultaneously representing a significant challenge encompassing complex international affairs and technological advancements.

sections.title: ⚠️ Awareness of the Climate Crisis and Societal Response
sections.content:
Public awareness and social participation are crucial in responding to the climate crisis, but warnings have been raised about the phenomenon of the climate crisis being easily forgotten due to 'ecological amnesia' [4]. Domestically, the climate change hidden behind the illusion of annual precipitation in the Jeju region [2] and the necessity of future countermeasures in the face of the climate crisis in the Incheon region are being emphasized [5]. This lack of awareness is also evident in political discourse on climate change, with some far-right politicians in the UK facing criticism for asserting that climate change should be 'enjoyed' or that it's 'not all doom and gloom' [29, 49, 52, 53, 63, 66, 70].

However, despite these challenges, calls for climate action are growing louder. The youth climate change group BigWave is conducting its regular recruitment for the second half of 2026, encouraging participation from younger generations [7], and in Hawaii, 13 youths filed a lawsuit against climate change, highlighting the importance of legal action [34]. Young African Catholics are also fighting climate change based on their faith, demonstrating calls for action from diverse segments of society [42].

Meanwhile, 20 years of research has proven that climate change has had a massive impact on Northern Canada [45], and the role of expert groups is expanding, with legal associations publishing new climate change guidelines for in-house lawyers [62]. Amidst political discussions on whether climate change will be reintroduced into educational curricula [61], arguments are being made that it is time to accept the necessity of urgent action on climate change, demanding improved awareness and proactive responses across society [58].

briefing.closing: The extreme climate phenomena discussed in today's briefing, the complex challenges of energy transition, and the societal awareness and response efforts clearly demonstrate the reality we face in this era of climate crisis. International cooperation and proactive implementation, both domestically and internationally, are more crucial than ever for a sustainable future. This concludes today's climate briefing.
